transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, what finally made me make an appointment and say something is that... lately, after I eat too much, I’ve been going upstairs and making myself throw up. And then I just come back down and act as if I’m just tidying the kitchen or getting ready for bed. I just felt like it was time I finally talked to someone about it.
During these episodes where you feel you have eaten too much, do you feel like you have lost control over your eating?

Yes, I really do. It’s... well, once I start, it feels like a switch just flips. It's almost like I’m watching myself keep eating, and there's a part of me in my head saying, ‘Linda, stop now,’ but my hands just keep reaching for more food. I just can't seem to stop it once it starts.
Besides making yourself throw up, have you ever used laxatives, diuretics, or other medications to try to control your weight after these episodes?
No, I haven't done anything like that. I don't take any laxatives or water pills or... any other medications to try and get rid of the food. It's really just making myself throw up.
How many times per week, on average, would you say these episodes of eating a large amount of food and then making yourself throw up occur?

Well, it's pretty frequent. I'd say... since last winter, there really hasn't been a week where I haven't had at least one of these, you know, private eating spells. And then after, I try to make up for it. Usually by throwing up, like I said, but sometimes I'll just skip meals the next day, or I'll go out and overdo it with my walking. But yeah, it's at least once a week, sometimes more.
How much does your body shape or your weight influence how you feel about yourself as a person?

I'm... I'm not really sure how to answer that, to be honest. I mean, I know I think about my weight, but I haven't really stopped to consider how much it actually changes how I feel about myself as a whole person. I guess I just haven't really looked at it that way or noticed a specific connection like that.
When you look in the mirror or think about your body, how much does your weight or your shape affect your self-esteem or how you feel about your worth as a person?

Well, it's... it's really just like I was saying a second ago. I mean, obviously I look in the mirror and I care about my size, but... if you're asking if it changes my actual worth as a person, I just don't know. I honestly haven't thought about my self-esteem in those exact terms, so I don't really have a better answer for you.
If you were to gain a few pounds, would that have a significant impact on how you feel about yourself or your day-to-day mood?

Yes, it absolutely would. I mean, my daughter and a woman from my church have both told me recently that I look too thin. But honestly, if my skirt feels even a little snug when I put it on, or if the scale goes up by just a single pound, I still panic. It's like... I feel as if I've somehow let myself become huge overnight. So, yes, it definitely has a big impact on my mood.
